ops.d: List every servers in the subscription.
List the servers in a resource group.

features.t: Servers (create, get, list, delete) over ARM
Virtual network rules
x: Microsoft.Sql/servers/virtualNetworkRules is a real ARM child resource: the subnet must exist and carry the Microsoft.Sql service endpoint (enabled for you from the console). The rule is not enforced against SQL connections: there is no network path to evaluate it against.

features.t: Databases (create, get, list, delete) over ARM
x: The subscription-wide "SQL databases" browse grid aggregates the native per-server Databases_List call across every known server (the ARM core's generic list does not scope by the server segment in the path) instead of calling a real Azure Resource Graph query, which is what the actual portal uses for this one blade.

features.t: Server firewall rules (Microsoft.Sql/servers/firewallRules)
Server public network access toggle
x: When publicNetworkAccess is Disabled, the azure-sql query data plane now rejects every connection with a 403 (matching real SQL servers, where disabling it blocks public-endpoint traffic outright). A caller that declares its network identity (request headers x-vyomi-source-ip / x-vyomi-source-subnet / x-vyomi-private-endpoint / x-vyomi-trusted-service, core/azure_netaccess.py) is checked against the server's firewall rules (start/end IP ranges, the 0.0.0.0 'Allow Azure services' rule for trusted services), virtualNetworkRules (subnet must carry the Microsoft.Sql service endpoint) and Approved private endpoint connections; a miss answers 403 ClientIpNotAllowed. A caller that declares nothing (the browser console) keeps the legacy behaviour - any connection succeeds while public access stays Enabled - because there is no real client network in a browser-only simulator.

features.t: Query editor (real SQL execution over the azure-sql data plane)
x: Runs on the same SqlStore seam as RDS/Cloud SQL (sqlite in Nano); T-SQL-specific syntax, stored procedures and SQL-authentication credential checks beyond a plain login/password string compare are not modelled.

features.t: "Use existing data: Sample" canned dataset load
x: Loads a small fixed Customer/Product/SalesOrderHeader schema with a few rows via the query data plane — not the real AdventureWorksLT sample database.

features.t: Compute + storage (service/compute tier, vCore auto-scaling, auto-pause, max size, zone redundancy)
x: maxSizeBytes is now enforced on the query data plane: once the database's real on-disk size (sqlite's own page accounting) reaches the configured cap, further INSERT/UPDATE/REPLACE statements are rejected with the real error 40544 (DatabaseSizeQuotaExceeded) until data is freed or the cap is raised. Service/compute tier, vCore auto-scaling, auto-pause and zone redundancy remain config-only — Vyomi does not enforce vCore limits, pause the compute, or model zone placement.

features.t: Transparent data encryption on/off, with a customer-managed Key Vault protector
x: properties.transparentDataEncryption.state round-trips through ARM, but data at rest is never actually encrypted or decrypted based on it. A customer-managed key (keyVaultKeyUri) IS enforced for real: the query data plane requires the database's system-assigned managed identity AND a real, enabled Key Vault key — disabling the key or removing the identity makes the database inaccessible (TdeProtectorUnavailable) until the key is re-enabled or the protector is switched back to service-managed. There is no Microsoft Entra permission check on top of that (Vyomi has no Key Vault access-policy/RBAC model) — only the key's own enabled state and the identity's presence are checked.

features.t: System-assigned managed identity
x: The identity block (including a generated principalId) round-trips through ARM and is now a real precondition for one feature: a customer-managed-key TDE protector is only honored while the database carries a system-assigned identity (azure.sql.transparent_data_encryption). It is still not usable for genuine Microsoft Entra authorization (RBAC role-assignment checks) to any other Vyomi service.

features.t: Automatic tuning options (FORCE_LAST_GOOD_PLAN, CREATE_INDEX, DROP_INDEX) and Performance recommendations
x: CREATE_INDEX recommendations are real: generated from the Query editor's own statement log by checking the SAME engine's EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for WHERE-equality lookups that need a table scan, shown on Performance recommendations with an Apply action that runs a real CREATE INDEX. When the automatic tuning option is On, matching recommendations are applied automatically instead of waiting for Apply. FORCE_LAST_GOOD_PLAN and DROP_INDEX stay config-only — no plan-regression detection or orphan-index pruning is modelled.

features.t: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to a database
x: Lock create/list/delete are real Microsoft.Authorization/locks over ARM at resource, resource-group and subscription scope (CanNotDelete/ReadOnly, name and notes validated); this blade manages the locks scoped to this SQL database only and has no scope switch. A resource-group or subscription lock really blocks writes and deletes of everything under it with 409 ScopeLocked (core/azure_arm_ext_core.py lock_conflict), but a lock set directly on a SQL database is stored and listed only: it does not block writes or deletes of the SQL database itself.

features.t: Activity log
x: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the timespan picker are not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.

features.t: Tags
Database export / import (.bacpac to and from Blob storage)
x: POST .../databases/{db}/export and .../databases/{db}/import or .../servers/{server}/import write / read the .bacpac in the simulator's OWN Azure Blob store. The storageUri host (<account>.blob.core.windows.net) is only parsed — the account must exist in the simulator (an ARM storage account or the emulator's devstoreaccount1) and the container must exist, otherwise the request fails; nothing is ever resolved on the internet.

features.t: Server connection policy (connectionPolicies/default)
x: The connection policy (Default / Proxy / Redirect) is stored on the server as a real connectionPolicies/default resource and returned to the SDK / az CLI. Vyomi's SQL front door is always a single endpoint, so Proxy and Redirect behave identically.

features.t: Dynamic Data Masking (dataMaskingPolicies/Default and its rules)
x: Masking is APPLIED to SELECT result sets for any login other than the server admin / exempt principals / users granted UNMASK (GRANT UNMASK TO user, REVOKE UNMASK FROM user). Functions: Default, Email, Number, Text/Custom, CCN, SSN. The login is the x-vyomi-sql-login header (TDS/Entra identity is not modelled).

features.t: Ledger (isLedgerOn at create)
x: Ledger tables (CREATE TABLE ... WITH (LEDGER = ON [(APPEND_ONLY = ON)]), or every table when the database is created with isLedgerOn): append-only tables reject UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE (37359); every write appends a block to a SHA-256 hash chain stored in the database with the table-state hash; row versions are kept in a ledger history; digests are generated and verify recomputes chain, digests and table state, detecting tampering outside the ledger path.

features.t: Maintenance window and event history
x: The configured maintenance window (maintenanceConfigurationId) is the database's real property; the event history is always empty because Vyomi never performs platform maintenance.

features.t: Add Azure AI Search (SQL)
x: A real search service, index, data source and indexer are created through Microsoft.Search, but Vyomi indexers only read Blob data: running the indexer on an azuresql data source ends in transientFailure with that message. Pulling table rows into an index is not implemented.

features.t: Data Discovery & Classification (column sensitivity labels)
x: A scan of the database's REAL tables classifies columns by name pattern and by sampled data (email, SSN, credit card with Luhn check, phone, IPv4 over up to 200 rows); labels persist as ARM sensitivityLabels and every SELECT that reads a labelled column writes dataSensitivityInformation into the audit record.

features.t: Copy database, point-in-time restore, restore dropped database
x: createMode Copy / PointInTimeRestore / Restore / RestoreLongTermRetentionBackup move real table data. PITR uses a base snapshot plus a write-ahead log of statements run through the data plane, so the restored state is exact to the statement; the log is in process memory (not durable across restart) and bulk bacpac imports are not logged.

features.t: Active geo-replication (secondary, replica links, failover, terminate)
x: Secondary databases are seeded from the primary and every later write is replayed on them synchronously; secondaries are read-only (error 3906); failover swaps roles, delete terminates the link. No replication lag, 'region' is a label; failover groups and Hyperscale named replicas are not modelled.

features.t: Short-term and long-term backup retention
x: Short-term retention (1-35 days, differential 12|24 h) bounds PITR; the LTR policy is validated (ISO-8601, 10-year cap) and one LTR backup artifact is taken when the policy is set, restorable and deletable. Weekly/monthly/yearly cadence is not scheduled.

features.t: Query Performance Insight (top queries by measured duration)
x: Built from the wall-clock timing and outcome of every statement run through the Vyomi SQL data plane (query editor / SDK). Not Query Store: no execution plans or wait stats, and no DTU/CPU metric because the engine has no resource governor. Auditing has no storage / Log Analytics / Event Hub destination.

features.t: Performance overview (statement counts, latency percentiles, size)
x: Built from the wall-clock timing and outcome of every statement run through the Vyomi SQL data plane (query editor / SDK). Not Query Store: no execution plans or wait stats, and no DTU/CPU metric because the engine has no resource governor. Auditing has no storage / Log Analytics / Event Hub destination.

features.t: Auditing (audit records of executed statements)
x: Built from the wall-clock timing and outcome of every statement run through the Vyomi SQL data plane (query editor / SDK). Not Query Store: no execution plans or wait stats, and no DTU/CPU metric because the engine has no resource governor. Auditing has no storage / Log Analytics / Event Hub destination.

features.t: SQL server: Access control (IAM) over ARM
x: Role assignments and the built-in role definitions are real ARM objects (Microsoft.Authorization) scoped to the server; the data-plane query path does not consult them (the simulator's single signed-in principal is not an Entra identity).
